previous_description: Obligation control requiring that a single actor who initiates a task must also complete it, preventing task hijacking or inconsistent workflow state that could be exploited by a different actor. Complements SeparationOfDuty by enforcing task continuity rather than task segregation. Anchored to NIST SP 800-53 CM-5 (Access Restrictions for Change) and workflow integrity controls.
definition: A procedural access constraint requiring that the actor who performs one step of a multi-step task or workflow also performs its designated follow-on steps, so that any attempt by a different actor to continue or complete that task instance is rejected.

distinguish_from.when: the rule requires that two steps be performed by different actors or roles, rather than by the same actor.
the check is a standalone predicate on a single request (e.g. resource.ownerId eq currentUser) with no link to a task instance the actor started.
access is restricted according to the actor's declared purpose rather than its participation in an earlier workflow step.
the logic is a general condition-plus-effect rule in a policy rather than a task-continuity obligation tied to workflow steps.

standard_reference: STS-ml Binding of Duties (BoD) organizational constraint; complements NIST SP 800-53 AC-5 Separation of Duties
code_evidence: a workflow or state-machine transition guard that compares the stored initiator, claimant or assignee of a task instance (e.g. startedBy, claimedBy) with the current user id and throws or returns 403 when they differ
BPMN/Camunda or similar workflow configuration that assigns a later user task to the process initiator (e.g. assignee="${initiator}") or locks a claimed task to a single user until completion
a dedicated exception or error message such as 'Only the user who started this request may submit it' or a class named like TaskOwnershipViolation or SameUserRequired raised in multi-step flows

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text explanation of which task steps are bound together and why the same actor must perform them; set it whenever the bound steps are not obvious from the element name.

attribute_descriptions.name: message
attribute_descriptions.description: The human-readable error or log message emitted when a different actor attempts to continue or complete the bound task, taken verbatim from the code where one exists.

notes: The CM-5 anchor is weak; no NIST 800-53 control names binding of duty, and STS-ml is the real source. There is no attribute listing the bound operations or steps, which the governs→resourceoperation relationship only partly covers. The constrains→role relationship implies role-level binding, while the definition is actor-level. Clarify the binding granularity.
